result.title: A Mesh to Remember: Persistent Appearance for Interactive Video Worlds
result.summary: Video world models synthesize photorealistic observations in response to user actions but struggle to remain consistent over long interactions. Coding agents and text-to-3D models instead generate explicit 3D worlds whose geometry and state persist by construction, but whose appearance falls far short of photorealism. Recent methods combine the strengths of both by rendering such worlds into coarse proxies that guide a video model. However, since these proxies only specify where things are, the renderer must invent what they look like as the world is explored, and anything it forgets is reinvented when a surface reappears. Our key insight is that a mesh identifies which surface each pixel shows, across frames and views, even as objects move, allowing it to serve as an address for what the renderer generates. We propose M2R (Mesh to Remember), a few-step causal video renderer that stores its own features on the surfaces they depict, in each object's frame, and retrieves them by rasterizing the mesh whenever those surfaces come back into view. Appearance thus travels with objects wherever they move, persists across revisits, and is shared by every agent that observes it, while memory grows with the surfaces seen instead of the number of frames. Trained only on synthetic data, M2R transfers zero-shot to real indoor scans and to worlds authored by coding agents. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods in consistency across static, dynamic, and multi-agent benchmarks, more than doubling object permanence and nearly doubling cross-agent consistency, while rendering 720p video in real time (40 FPS).

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 M2R：把视频渲染器自身特征存放在所描绘的网格表面上（按各物体自身坐标系），表面重新进入视野时通过光栅化网格取回，从而让外观随物体移动、跨重访与跨智能体保持一致；仅用合成数据训练即可零样本迁移到真实室内扫描与代码智能体构建的世界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以表面身份而非帧序寻址的持久特征缓存」可能为 LVR 中视觉证据跨视角留存、以及 latent 检索中位置/缓存/注意力结构的影响提供概念参照，但该工作面向渲染一致性而非推理，线索尚需核查。
